micronarrative: I view the backlash against the bakery as wrong, akin to blackmailing a business for its religion. As an agnostic and gay person, I strongly disagree with Chick-fil-A’s Christianity, yet I would never go out of my way to blackmail them; I simply boycott by not buying their products. I find it baffling that some Gen Z LGBTQ individuals eat there to fit in, ignoring the discrimination. Growing up in Phoenix, I attended church out of obligation because my parents were Catholic, but I always felt resistant to doing things for the sake of tradition. I pretended to be attentive as a kid, but deep down, I wanted nothing to do with it. I am not the type to try and fit in just to please people. Therefore, I see the bakery as brave for choosing authenticity over conformity. They have a right to express their religious views, and I support that stance against performative pressure.
